findings.evidence: ParityOdd.lean:346-368 declares only `aOfBasis`, `aOfBasis_eq_det` (not `@[simp]`) and `parityOddAssumptions_aOfBasis`; the `conserved_left` field is the sole annihilation statement. BilinMap.lean:69-79 has the simp lemmas that would apply if the body were visible. Basic.lean:288-311 gives the leptonic side all six.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` lemmas `aOfBasis_apply_p_left_eq_zero`, `aOfBasis_apply_p_right_eq_zero`, `aOfBasis_apply_q_left_eq_zero`, `aOfBasis_apply_q_right_eq_zero` and `aOfBasis_apply_self`, each one line from `AlternatingMap.bilinMap_apply_left_eq_zero ![K.p, K.q] 0/1` etc., mirroring `Leptonic.lMuNuOdd_apply_k_left_eq_zero` … `lMuNuOdd_apply_self`. Cleanest: split off `aOfForm (ε : V [⋀^Fin 4]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) K := ε.bilinMap ![K.p, K.q]` carrying those lemmas (nothing in them uses the basis) and set `aOfBasis b K := aOfForm b.det K`; that also gives the hadronic counterpart of `lMuNuOdd` that the Layer 1.1 `L^{μν}W_{μν}` contraction needs with a shared `ε`.
findings.issue: `aOfBasis` has no lemma for its annihilation of `K.p` (nor simp forms for `K.q` or the diagonal). The module is `public section` without `@[expose]` (line 79), so the body is hidden and the `AlternatingMap.bilinMap_apply_left_eq_zero` / `_right_eq_zero` / `bilinMap_apply_self` simp lemmas cannot fire on `aOfBasis b K K.p w`. The only route to `A K.p v = 0` is `ParityOddAssumptions.apply_p_eq_zero`, which needs `g.IsSymm` plus `SpectatorPartners` — hypotheses `aOfBasis` does not require. Roadmap convention 6 names annihilation of `p` and `q` as a defining property of `A`.

findings.evidence: ParityOdd.lean:426-427 `aFour K := aOfBasis (Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin 4)) K`; 430-432 `aFour_eq_det … := aOfBasis_eq_det ..`; 448-450 `parityOddAssumptions_aFour … := parityOddAssumptions_aOfBasis g (Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin 4)) K`.
findings.fix: Drop `aFour`, `aFour_eq_det` and `parityOddAssumptions_aFour`; state `aFour_kFour_apply` and the witness results about `aOfBasis (Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin 4)) kFour` directly. If a short witness name is wanted, keep `aFour` specialised to `kFour` only and delete the two duplicated general lemmas.
findings.issue: `Witness.aFour` is a bare specialization of `aOfBasis` (`aOfBasis (Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin 4)) K`), and `aFour_eq_det` / `parityOddAssumptions_aFour` are literal re-exports of `aOfBasis_eq_det` / `parityOddAssumptions_aOfBasis`. This publishes a second canonical name for the same object on `ℝ⁴`, with two duplicate lemmas, so downstream statements can be written against either and will not rewrite into each other without unfolding (the body is not exposed).

findings.evidence: ParityOdd.lean:79 `public section` (no `@[expose]`); 408-418 define `kFour` with `pPrime`, `k`, `kPrime` and export only `kFour_p`, `kFour_q`. Contrast Basic.lean:82 `@[expose] public section` covering `kWit` (Basic.lean:1271-1281).
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] lemma kFour_k : kFour.k = ![0, 0, 0, 1] := (rfl)`, `kFour_kPrime` and `kFour_pPrime`, matching the `(rfl)` style already used for `kFour_p`/`kFour_q`.
findings.issue: `kFour` has five fields but only `kFour_p` and `kFour_q` accessor lemmas, and the module is `public section` without `@[expose]`, so `kFour.k`, `kFour.kPrime` and `kFour.pPrime` are unreachable downstream — the values cannot be recovered without unfolding. (The analogous `kWit` in `Tensors/Basic.lean` gets away with two lemmas only because that file is `@[expose] public section`.) The roadmap's four-dimensional acceptance example contracts the leptonic tensor against this witness and needs the lepton momenta.

summary: The parity-odd core (`ParityOddAssumptions`, `exists_half_turn`, `SpectatorPair`/`SpectatorPlane`, the uniqueness theorems) is well shaped and `@[ext]`-clean, but `aOfBasis` ships without the annihilation lemmas that characterise it while its body is unexposed, and the `Witness` section re-exports `aOfBasis` under a second name with duplicate lemmas and an incomplete accessor set for `kFour`.
